definition: a short way to start a status report
example: Quick update on the login bug: we found the cause this morning.
exampleEs: Una actualización rápida sobre el error de inicio de sesión: encontramos la causa esta mañana.
cloze: Quick ____ on the login bug: we found the cause this morning.
collocations: Short update on X in Slack: ...
note: Say 'update on', not 'update of'.

definition: introduces the current status of a task
example: Here's where we are on the migration: we moved two services.
exampleEs: Así vamos con la migración: ya movimos dos servicios.
cloze: Here's where we ____ on the migration: we moved two services.
collocations: Let me tell you where we stand on...

definition: we will finish on time if nothing changes
example: We're on track to release the new dashboard on Friday.
exampleEs: Vamos bien para lanzar el nuevo panel el viernes.
cloze: We're on ____ to release the new dashboard on Friday.

definition: politely says that a task is late
example: We're a bit behind on testing, but we can catch up by Tuesday.
exampleEs: Vamos un poco atrasados con las pruebas, pero podemos ponernos al día el martes.
cloze: We're a bit ____ on testing, but we can catch up by Tuesday.
collocations: X is running a bit late.
note: Add how you will catch up: it sounds more professional.

definition: we cannot continue until something else happens
example: We're blocked on the API keys from the security team.
exampleEs: Estamos bloqueados esperando las claves de la API del equipo de seguridad.
cloze: We're ____ on the API keys from the security team.
collocations: We're waiting on X before we can...
note: 'Blocked on' + the thing you need; 'blocked by' + the person or problem.

headword: the main thing to flag is
es: lo principal que quiero señalar es
definition: introduces the most important risk or problem
example: The main thing to flag is that the budget may not be approved this month.
exampleEs: Lo principal que quiero señalar es que quizá no aprueben el presupuesto este mes.
cloze: The main thing to ____ is that the budget may not be approved this month.
collocations: The main thing to flag is...
One risk I want to highlight is...
note: To flag = to point out a problem so people notice it.

definition: the middle part of a standup update: what you are doing now
example: Last week I finished the report; this week I'm working on the export feature.
exampleEs: La semana pasada terminé el reporte; esta semana estoy trabajando en la función de exportar.
cloze: Last week I finished the report; this week I'm ____ on the export feature.
collocations: This week I'm working on Y.
note: Standup formula: finished (past), working on (now), blocked by (problem).

definition: you understand and accept the idea
example: That makes sense, so let's test it with real users first.
exampleEs: Tiene sentido, así que probémoslo primero con usuarios reales.
cloze: That ____ sense, so let's test it with real users first.
note: Not 'that has sense': in English, things make sense.

definition: you agree with a plan and will support it
example: I'm on board with that, as long as we keep the deadline.
exampleEs: Estoy de acuerdo con eso, siempre y cuando mantengamos la fecha límite.
cloze: I'm on ____ with that, as long as we keep the deadline.
collocations: You have my support on this.

definition: you accept that the other person's idea is reasonable
example: Fair point, we didn't think about the cost of the servers.
exampleEs: Buen punto, no pensamos en el costo de los servidores.
cloze: Fair ____, we didn't think about the cost of the servers.

headword: I agree, and I'd add that
es: estoy de acuerdo, y añadiría que
definition: agree and then give one more idea
example: I agree, and I'd add that we need better logs.
exampleEs: Estoy de acuerdo, y añadiría que necesitamos mejores logs.
cloze: I agree, and I'd ____ that we need better logs.
collocations: I agree, and I'd add that...
note: Agree first, then add: it sounds positive, not competitive.

definition: a friendly way to say yes
example: Thursday at ten? Sounds good to me.
exampleEs: ¿El jueves a las diez? Me parece bien.
cloze: Thursday at ten? ____ good to me.
note: In Slack people often write SGTM.

headword: I see where you're coming from, but
definition: shows respect before you disagree
example: I see where you're coming from, but I think the risk is too high.
exampleEs: Entiendo tu punto, pero creo que el riesgo es demasiado alto.
cloze: I see where you're ____ from, but I think the risk is too high.
collocations: I see where you're coming from, but...

headword: I'm not sure that would work because
es: no estoy seguro de que funcione porque
definition: a soft way to disagree and give a reason
example: I'm not sure that would work because the client needs it in English.
exampleEs: No estoy seguro de que funcione porque el cliente lo necesita en inglés.
cloze: I'm not sure that would ____ because the client needs it in English.
collocations: I'm not sure that would work because...
I have some doubts about this because...
note: Always give the reason after 'because'.

headword: could we look at it another way?
definition: invites a different solution without saying no
example: Could we look at it another way? Maybe we don't need a new tool.
exampleEs: ¿Podríamos verlo de otra forma? Quizá no necesitamos una herramienta nueva.
cloze: Could we look at it ____ way? Maybe we don't need a new tool.
collocations: Could we look at it another way?
Is there another option we could consider?
note: 'Another way', not 'other way'.

headword: I have a slightly different take
es: tengo una opinión un poco distinta
definition: says your opinion is different, politely
example: I have a slightly different take: the problem is the process, not the people.
exampleEs: Tengo una opinión un poco distinta: el problema es el proceso, no las personas.
cloze: I have a slightly different ____: the problem is the process, not the people.
collocations: I have a slightly different take.
I see it a little differently.
note: A take = an opinion (informal).

es: lo que me preocupa es que
definition: names a risk without blaming anyone
example: My concern is that we are testing too late in the sprint.
exampleEs: Lo que me preocupa es que estamos probando demasiado tarde en el sprint.
cloze: My ____ is that we are testing too late in the sprint.

definition: politely interrupts someone
example: Sorry to jump in, but we only have five minutes left.
exampleEs: Perdón por interrumpir, pero solo nos quedan cinco minutos.
cloze: Sorry to ____ in, but we only have five minutes left.
collocations: If I could just come in here...

definition: asks for a turn to speak
example: Can I add something here? The data from last month tells a different story.
exampleEs: ¿Puedo añadir algo aquí? Los datos del mes pasado cuentan otra historia.
cloze: Can I ____ something here? The data from last month tells a different story.

headword: just a quick point on that
es: solo un punto rápido sobre eso
definition: says you will speak briefly about the current topic
example: Just a quick point on that: the license costs more in Europe.
exampleEs: Solo un punto rápido sobre eso: la licencia cuesta más en Europa.
cloze: Just a ____ point on that: the license costs more in Europe.
collocations: Just a quick point on that.

definition: politely stops someone from interrupting you
example: Sorry, may I finish my point? I'm almost done.
exampleEs: Perdón, ¿me dejas terminar mi idea? Ya casi acabo.
cloze: Sorry, may I ____ my point? I'm almost done.
collocations: Let me just finish this thought.
note: Use it calmly: it helps you get interrupted less.

headword: just to make sure I understand
es: solo para asegurarme de que entiendo
definition: starts checking that you understood correctly
example: Just to make sure I understand, you want the report by Monday, right?
exampleEs: Solo para asegurarme de que entiendo, quieres el reporte para el lunes, ¿verdad?
cloze: Just to make ____ I understand, you want the report by Monday, right?
collocations: Just to make sure I understand, you're saying...
note: Repeat their idea in your words: it is the best tool for a non-native speaker.

definition: asks someone to repeat
example: Sorry, the connection is bad. Could you say that again?
exampleEs: Perdón, la conexión está mal. ¿Podrías repetirlo?
cloze: Sorry, the connection is bad. Could you say that ____?

definition: asks for the meaning of a word or idea
example: What do you mean by 'quick win'?
exampleEs: ¿A qué te refieres con 'quick win'?
cloze: What do you ____ by 'quick win'?
collocations: Could you clarify what you mean by...?
note: Not 'what do you want to say with': that is Spanish word order.

headword: do you mean X or Y?
definition: offers two options to check meaning
example: Do you mean this Friday or next Friday?
exampleEs: ¿Te refieres a este viernes o al próximo?
cloze: Do you ____ this Friday or next Friday?
collocations: Do you mean X or Y?
Are you referring to X or Y?

definition: you say your idea again in different words
example: Let me rephrase that: we need one owner for each task.
exampleEs: Déjame decirlo de otra forma: necesitamos un responsable para cada tarea.
cloze: Let me ____ that: we need one owner for each task.
collocations: Let me put it another way.
note: Useful when you see confused faces.

definition: asks for a moment before answering
example: That's a big change. Let me think about that and reply tomorrow.
exampleEs: Es un cambio grande. Déjame pensarlo y te respondo mañana.
cloze: That's a big change. Let me ____ about that and reply tomorrow.
collocations: I'd like to give that some thought.

headword: let me get back to you
definition: promises an answer later
example: Good question. Let me get back to you after I check the numbers.
exampleEs: Buena pregunta. Déjame revisar los números y te respondo.
cloze: Good question. Let me get ____ to you after I check the numbers.
collocations: Let me get back to you on that.
I'll come back to you with an answer by...
note: Say when: 'by tomorrow' makes it a real promise.

headword: I don't have the number at hand
es: no tengo el número a la mano
definition: the information is not with you right now
example: I don't have the number at hand; I'll follow up by email.
exampleEs: No tengo el número a la mano; te lo mando por correo.
cloze: I don't have the number at ____; I'll follow up by email.
collocations: I don't have the number at hand.
I don't have that figure with me right now.
note: Spanish 'a la mano' = English 'at hand'.

definition: starts a step-by-step explanation
example: Let me walk you through the new deployment process.
exampleEs: Déjame explicarte paso a paso el nuevo proceso de despliegue.
cloze: Let me ____ you through the new deployment process.
collocations: I'll take you through it step by step.

headword: as you can see on this slide
es: como pueden ver en esta diapositiva
definition: points the audience to the screen
example: As you can see on this slide, sign-ups doubled in March.
exampleEs: Como pueden ver en esta diapositiva, los registros se duplicaron en marzo.
cloze: As you can see on this ____, sign-ups doubled in March.
collocations: As you can see on this slide, ...
If you look at this chart, ...
note: On a slide, in a chart, on the screen.

headword: to sum up what we agreed
definition: starts a short summary of the decisions at the end
example: To sum up what we agreed, we fix the bug first and release on Friday.
exampleEs: Para resumir lo que acordamos, primero arreglamos el error y lanzamos el viernes.
cloze: To sum up what we ____, we fix the bug first and release on Friday.
collocations: To sum up what we agreed, ...
So, in summary, we decided to...
note: Ends a meeting clearly: everyone hears the same decisions.

definition: names the one idea people should remember
example: The key takeaway is that users want speed more than new features.
exampleEs: La idea clave es que los usuarios quieren velocidad más que funciones nuevas.
cloze: The ____ takeaway is that users want speed more than new features.
collocations: The main point to remember is...

definition: checks the audience before you continue
example: That's the first part. Any questions so far?
exampleEs: Esa es la primera parte. ¿Alguna pregunta hasta ahora?
cloze: That's the first part. Any questions so ____?
collocations: Does that all make sense so far?

definition: starts the list of actions at the end of a meeting
example: So the next steps are: Ana updates the design and I write the tests.
exampleEs: Entonces los siguientes pasos son: Ana actualiza el diseño y yo escribo las pruebas.
cloze: So the next ____ are: Ana updates the design and I write the tests.
note: Say who does what: one owner per step.

definition: asks someone to own a task
example: We need someone to check the contracts. Who can take that on?
exampleEs: Necesitamos a alguien que revise los contratos. ¿Quién puede encargarse de eso?
cloze: We need someone to check the contracts. Who can ____ that on?
collocations: Would anyone like to own this?
note: Take on = accept a task or responsibility.

headword: I'll send a summary after this call
es: enviaré un resumen después de esta llamada
definition: promises written notes after the meeting
example: Thanks, everyone. I'll send a summary after this call.
exampleEs: Gracias a todos. Enviaré un resumen después de esta llamada.
cloze: Thanks, everyone. I'll send a ____ after this call.
collocations: I'll send a summary after this call.
I'll circulate the notes this afternoon.

definition: agrees to discuss a topic again at a later meeting
example: Let's circle back on this next week when we have the data.
exampleEs: Retomemos esto la próxima semana cuando tengamos los datos.
cloze: Let's circle back on this ____ week when we have the data.
collocations: Let's circle back on this next week.
Let's revisit this at our next meeting.

es: te perdí en, dejé de entenderte en
definition: says where you stopped understanding
example: Sorry, I lost you at the part about the database.
exampleEs: Perdón, te perdí en la parte de la base de datos.
cloze: Sorry, I ____ you at the part about the database.
collocations: Could you go back to the part about...?
Lost you at X, can you repeat?
note: Name the exact part: it is faster than 'I don't understand'.

headword: could you slow down a little?
definition: asks someone to speak more slowly
example: Could you slow down a little? My English is better at a calmer speed.
exampleEs: ¿Podrías hablar un poco más despacio? Mi inglés es mejor a un ritmo más tranquilo.
cloze: Could you ____ down a little? My English is better at a calmer speed.
collocations: Could you slow down a little?
Would you mind speaking a bit more slowly?
note: Nobody minds this request; native speakers forget they talk fast.

definition: asks to see what the other person sees
example: I can't follow the numbers. Could you share your screen?
exampleEs: No puedo seguir los números. ¿Podrías compartir tu pantalla?
cloze: I can't follow the numbers. Could you ____ your screen?
collocations: Would you mind sharing your screen?

definition: asks for written text during a call
example: Could you paste the link in the chat?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías pegar el enlace en el chat?
cloze: Could you ____ the link in the chat?
collocations: Could you paste it in the chat?
Could you drop the link in the chat?
note: Written text helps when audio is hard to follow.

definition: opens the meeting
example: It's ten past, so let's get started.
exampleEs: Ya son y diez, así que empecemos.
cloze: It's ten past, so let's get ____.

definition: checks that screen sharing works
example: Can everyone see my screen? I'm sharing the roadmap.
exampleEs: ¿Todos ven mi pantalla? Estoy compartiendo el roadmap.
cloze: Can everyone ____ my screen? I'm sharing the roadmap.
collocations: Sharing now, can you see it?

definition: tells someone that nobody can hear them
example: Carlos, I think you're on mute.
exampleEs: Carlos, creo que tienes el micrófono apagado.
cloze: Carlos, I think you're on ____.
collocations: I think your mic is off.

definition: checks agreement on a time or plan
example: Let's move the demo to Thursday. Does that work for everyone?
exampleEs: Movamos la demo al jueves. ¿A todos les funciona?
cloze: Let's move the demo to Thursday. Does that ____ for everyone?

definition: suggests discussing a topic later with fewer people
example: This is getting very detailed, so let's take this offline.
exampleEs: Esto se está volviendo muy detallado, así que hablemos de esto aparte.
cloze: This is getting very detailed, so let's take this ____.
note: Offline here does not mean without internet: it means outside this meeting.

headword: can we put a pin in that?
definition: pauses a topic to come back to it later
example: Good idea, but can we put a pin in that until the next sprint?
exampleEs: Buena idea, pero ¿lo dejamos pendiente hasta el próximo sprint?
cloze: Good idea, but can we put a ____ in that until the next sprint?
collocations: Can we put a pin in that?

definition: promises a short update
example: I'll keep it short because we're almost out of time.
exampleEs: Seré breve porque ya casi no tenemos tiempo.
cloze: I'll keep it ____ because we're almost out of time.

headword: I'm afraid I can't make it
definition: politely says you cannot attend
example: I'm afraid I can't make it to the 3 p.m. call; can we move it?
exampleEs: Me temo que no podré llegar a la llamada de las 3; ¿podemos moverla?
cloze: I'm afraid I can't ____ it to the 3 p.m. call; can we move it?
collocations: I'm afraid I can't make it.
Unfortunately I won't be able to attend.
note: Make it = be able to attend or arrive.

headword: could you give me an example?
definition: asks for a concrete case
example: I'm not sure I follow. Could you give me an example?
exampleEs: No estoy seguro de entender. ¿Me puedes dar un ejemplo?
cloze: I'm not sure I follow. Could you give me an ____?
collocations: Could you give me an example?
What would that look like in practice?

definition: everyone gives a short update in turn
example: Let's go around the table and hear from each team.
exampleEs: Hagamos una ronda y escuchemos a cada equipo.
cloze: Let's go ____ the table and hear from each team.
note: Works on video calls too.

definition: invites a quiet person to speak
example: I'd like to hear from Priya, since she tested it.
exampleEs: Me gustaría escuchar a Priya, ya que ella lo probó.
cloze: I'd like to ____ from Priya, since she tested it.

definition: the meeting will end soon
example: We're running out of time, so let's decide in the chat.
exampleEs: Se nos acaba el tiempo, así que decidamos en el chat.
cloze: We're ____ out of time, so let's decide in the chat.

es: yo me encargo de, yo lidero
definition: volunteers to own a task
example: I'll take the lead on the security review.
exampleEs: Yo me encargo de la revisión de seguridad.
cloze: I'll take the ____ on the security review.
